lessons: Separate grasp miss, slip and occlusion: require visible key motion relative to the table and consistency relative to the gripper before declaring retention.
Fresh point identity is an execution prerequisite. After a stale-point interruption, inspect the actual partially moved robot and reobserve before replanning.
Small reprojection or outline-fit residuals do not validate feature identity, support height or physical pad contact.
Endpoint IK is not a reachable, economical trajectory. Budget from reported kinematic expansion and measured action consumption, not requested steps.
Partial native credit does not identify a completed subgoal; maintain an evidence-based ledger for acquisition, transfer, insertion and turn.
The slow-lift/long-settle candidate still achieved no native success; further slowing alone is not a supported remedy.
Seed 2 demonstrates terminal non-possession, not the timing or mechanism of grasp failure. Do not relabel a possible miss as confirmed slip.
Hypothesis: nominal grasp-center targeting leaves the thin shaft outside an effective opposing-pad region, even when TCP tracking is accurate.
A reconstructed bow center can support pose estimation but may lie in empty space; it is not automatically a valid physical contact target.
Budget both native actions and remaining inspection submissions. Camera repositioning consumed 24 actions in seed 0 despite an eight-step request.
Partial scores do not identify completed subgoals, and finish only holds for evaluation.
